## Firefox and Netflix
Firefox has no tab-capture feature, so the Firefox version attaches to the page's video player instead. Firefox's own code allows add-ons to process copy-protected audio such as Netflix, but this couldn't be tested on Netflix itself. So the add-on checks for itself:
- If a site blocks it, the video goes quiet. Within about 5 seconds the add-on turns itself off, tells you in the popup, and offers **Reload page** to bring the sound back. It won't try that site again unless you choose **Try again on this site**.
- It only attaches once Firefox's audio engine is running. If it says *"click once anywhere on the video page"*, do that and it finishes turning on by itself.
- Changing Netflix's own volume slider still works, and it teaches the add-on.
